# Circle

> An issue tracker where people and agents write to the same data in real time.
> Built on Ablo (write path + sync stream) over Neon Postgres, with Drizzle for
> migrations, Better Auth for identity, eve for the agent runtime, and Next.js 15
> / React 19 / Tailwind v4 / shadcn/ui for the interface. Not a front-end
> template: every list reads live and every mutation is a synchronised write.

Key facts for coding agents:

- **The one rule: any change to workspace data is an Ablo write.** Never a
  Zustand action, never a direct Postgres write from a route. A write that skips
  Ablo looks identical to the person who made it and reaches nobody else. The
  deliberate exceptions are identity (Better Auth via Drizzle), `db/seed.ts`,
  and the issue-number counter in `app/api/issues`.
- **Verify in two browsers, not with a reload.** The data is usually in the
  database either way; what breaks is the live read. Four surfaces shipped
  writing to memory before this was the rule.
- Reads: `hooks/use-workspace-data.ts` exposes synchronous live reads off the
  synced local pool (`useIssues`, `useProjects`, `useSavedViews`,
  `useTeamDocuments`, `useAgentChats`, …). They stay reactive in render.
- Writes: one hook per model — `use-issue-actions`, `use-initiative-actions`,
  `use-document-actions`, `use-view-actions`, `use-comment-actions`,
  `use-workflow-state-actions`, `use-project-detail-actions`,
  `use-issue-link-actions`, `use-cycle-actions`, `use-label-actions`.
- `ablo/schema.ts` is the contract: models, which sync group each row fans out
  on (`orgScoped` / `teamScoped`), and how a signed-in person maps to groups.
  `app/api/ablo-session/route.ts` mints the browser's credential and is the only
  place capabilities are granted — a capability's operations are fixed at mint,
  so no UI can work around a missing one.
- Drizzle owns all DDL (`db/schema/`, `db/migrations/`). Ablo never migrates.
  After a schema change: `ablo push`, then `pnpm ablo:reload`, then test a write.
- Agent: `agent/` holds the eve agent `scout`, its tools and its instructions.
  `agent/lib/circle.ts` `loadRun` mints a per-run session scoped to that run's
  team and org. The model only ever sees a run id — it cannot name a team, an
  issue or a capability.
- `lib/domain/` holds the domain types (`Issue`, `Project`, `Cycle`, `Status`,
  `Priority`), the icon and priority registries, new-workspace defaults, and the
  fixtures `db/seed.ts` turns into rows. No view reads a fixture at render time;
  every list reads live off the Ablo pool.
- Ablo API conventions, all in `AI_GUIDE.md`: narrow a server read by a
  reference field with `listAllWhere` rather than `where`, which is for scalar
  columns; `delete()` takes `{ id }`; clearing a field is `null`, since
  `undefined` means leave it alone; take the organization id from the session
  rather than off a row, because `.from()`-mapped fields are only present on
  rows written through Ablo; rows seeded straight into Postgres need
  `ablo_tenant_id` stamped by `pnpm db:backfill` before they reach a client.
- Tests: `pnpm test:unit` (pure logic, instant) and `pnpm test:e2e` (drives the
  real UI against a production build and a seeded database, asserting against
  Postgres through `tests/helpers/db.ts`). e2e needs Ablo credentials so it is a
  pre-release step, not CI. Assert against the database, never against the
  screen you just wrote to, and verify a new test by breaking the code and
  watching it fail.
- `lib/features.ts` flags surfaces that exist but are off — Reviews and the
  integrations settings both render fixtures or connect to nothing. Switching
  one off means the nav entry stops being a link *and* the route calls
  `notFound()`.
- URLs are `/{orgId}/…` where `orgId` is the workspace slug, taken from the URL
  or `useWorkspace().organizationSlug`. Never hardcode it.

Docs: `README.md` (getting started), `AI_GUIDE.md` (where each kind of logic
lives, and the Ablo conventions), `DEPLOY.md` (production).
